title: Backrooms: fresh air and boss fashion
summary: Keep the vents running, pick a bigger Endless crew, and dress up your Boss Builder mannequin.
changes: New REFRESH VENTS button on the monitor. Let the air run out and you pass out, and the vents clog faster every night. Boss fights skip it. The night-1 tutorial now covers it.
Endless runs start with 3 specimens on Easy, 4 on Normal and 5 on Hard.
6 AM now goes straight to the end screen.
Boss Builder has a new LOOK tab: height, build, head, arm and leg size, ten faces, hats, tops, bottoms and colours. Share codes include the look.

title: Arcade Tycoon 2.0
summary: A complete remake with six venues, 17 attractions and much smarter visitors.
changes: Visitors now have tastes, budgets and needs: hunger, thirst, restrooms and rest.
New attractions, service buildings and decor, plus staff, improvements, campaigns, random events and daily reports.
Your lifetime earnings and venue carry over; your old floor is refunded as cash.

title: Pocket Heist: a new crew
summary: Rebuilt from the ground up with ten chapters of new security and a safehouse shop.
changes: 100 procedurally built jobs, then endless heists. Your cleared-job count carries over.
Cameras, lasers, keycards, vaults, dark rooms, lockers, guard dogs, creaky floors and terminals.
Spend your take on smoke bombs, noisemakers, EMPs and stealth gear.

title: Ricochet Club: eight new clubs
summary: 80 new tables with bumpers, glass, portals, switches, sand, gravity wells and pockets.
changes: Every table is generated from a real, replayable solution.
Par-based three-star ratings and a shot preview.
Endless tables continue after the final club.

title: Parcel Panic: routes and daily deliveries
summary: Three modes, new crate types and tools.
changes: 60 delivery routes with goals: priority boxes, taped crates and dispatch quotas.
A Daily route everyone shares, plus endless Classic.
Box cutter, forklift and new-order tools earned through streaks and bonus stamps.

title: Odd Hours: the full collection
summary: Eight cameras, seven nights and endless Overtime.
changes: Seven anomaly categories to report, from moved objects to things that watch you.
Archive photos are now limited, and reports take time to file.
Subtler changes on later nights.

title: Backrooms: For Science is out
summary: Backrooms: For Science moves from Playtest into the main library.
changes: Now playable from the main arcade as the third game.

title: Neon Slip: The Warden arrives
summary: A modular boss with randomized attacks can intercept your run.
changes: A fresh 25% boss roll at every 1,000 score. A successful roll waits for the current obstacle wave to clear.
Four destructible modules are chosen from eight weapons: scatter cannons, railguns, rockets, mortars, saw racks, arc gates, helix cannons, and drone bays. Destroy every module to expose the core.
Get a temporary Twin Pulse, Burst Driver, or Ion Lance, automatic firing, three combat hull points, and a full Dash charge. Rockets and drones can be shot down.
Earn +60 score per module and +400 for the core. The gun disarms after victory and your normal route resumes.

title: Neon Slip: a smoother flight
summary: A fresh flight console, flowing trails, and sharper feedback throughout every run.
changes: New neon menu and compact HUD, a layered starfield, ship banking, connected engine trails, and redesigned pickups.
Dash shockwaves, phase-break bursts, shield rings, multiplier popups, immediate close-call feedback, and new flight sound effects.
Consistent simulation timing across refresh rates, immediate keyboard reversals, bounded visual effects, and support for reduced motion and the Chromebook profile.

title: Neon Slip: five new hazards
summary: Ten distinct encounters now shuffle into each run.
changes: Added crushing jaws, proximity mines with warning flashes, diagonal comet rain, live electric rails, and bouncing wrecking balls.
New encounters share the existing shield, dash, spark, and close-call systems. Classic keeps its original obstacles.

title: A sneak peek at what’s next
summary: The News tab is a public feed from Rhett.
changes: Rhett can publish descriptions and up to three snapshots per post using the owner account. Everyone can read the feed.
Snapshots are resized before upload, drafts survive reloads, and published posts are stored online across browsers.

title: Square Off 2: more of the music
summary: Updated music loops retain more of each track.
changes: Revised loop points for Standard, Endless and Training; Endless keeps its opening build and a longer main loop.
Updated quiet-gap handling near the beginning of a loop.

title: Square Off 2 enters the Arcade
summary: The playable sequel is now beside Square Off in the main collection.
changes: Play the ten-round Standard Run, Endless, Practice Workshop and Tutorial with twelve playable squares.
Moved out of the Admin Tab, preserving its cover and personal quote. Its separate progress now joins Arcade password saves.

title: A new home for your progress
summary: Your Stats has been rebuilt with a clear overview, 76 achievements and a searchable game-record collection.
changes: Separate Overview, Achievements and Game records sections keep playtime, recent games and milestones easy to find.
Expanded from 17 to 76 achievements, with progress bars, game filters, search and unlocked milestones that stay with your save password.
Added genre playtime, your next milestones, collection exploration, last-played dates, and more information from saved game records. Existing playtime and achievements are preserved.

title: Ducks vs. Dogs 2 joins the flock
summary: The cartoony 3D sequel is now right beside the original in the library.
changes: Collect 34 ducks, unlock five shops, and defend six worlds with a loadout that grows from five to eight duck types.
Includes Quack Power, challenge levels and unlockable Endless Pond and Boss Rumble modes. Progress uses its own save and is included in arcade password saves.

title: Waves, rings and smoother flights
summary: Meridian gains animated seas, methane lakes, detailed rings and flight improvements.
changes: Added moving water, floating capsules and swimming astronauts, with polar methane lakes on Titan and Lantern.
Updated planetary rings, ring shadows and close-up particles, plus cloud and terrain transitions.
Improved exhaust and flight trajectory displays, removed the EVA jetpack fuel limit, and added crash reports and graphics-reset recovery.

title: New clouds and interstellar names
summary: Meridian Space Program has new clouds across more worlds and fresh names for interstellar planets.
changes: Added distinct cloud layers, colors and winds for rocky worlds and gas giants, lit by each world's local star.
Updated interstellar planet names and matching mission text while preserving existing saves and mission progress.

title: Meridian Space Program is ready for launch
summary: Build rockets, earn science and explore. Now playable from the second row of the library.
changes: The existing Meridian card now opens the full game, including its blueprint editor, research, missions and space exploration.
Program progress and quicksaves are included in password saves. The original artwork and Rhett’s quote are preserved.

title: Lights back on solid ground
summary: Slide lights now attach to the surface instead of floating above the removed rails.
changes: Moved lamp bases just inside the slide edges and embedded them slightly in the surface.
Tilted each light with the local slide surface, including banked turns.

title: Open sides, launch pads restored
summary: The yellow side railings are gone; the launch pads are back.
changes: Removed continuous yellow side rails and the player wall effect, so you can steer or jump off either edge anywhere.
Restored gold launch strips, arches, landing markings and their original extra lift and directional boosts.
Jumping off ordinary sections remains available, and the green landing guide stays active in the air.

title: Jump off anywhere
summary: Slide Between no longer needs yellow launch pads.
changes: Removed yellow launch strips, arches and location-specific jump boosts.
Jump or Space gives a full-strength leap anywhere on the slide, with steering in the air.
Updated the instructions and shortcut count; the green landing guide still appears while airborne.

title: A cleaner start in Slide Between
summary: Start on a random map from the existing collection.
changes: Excluded the basic first layout from play. Existing layouts and their best-time records are preserved.
Removed map labels and previews from the menu and results.
Unfinished rounds retain their current map when reopened.

title: A new map after every round
summary: Slide Between automatically rotates courses after every win or loss.
changes: The next round always uses a different course, whether you win, lose to the robot, or fall.
Removed manual map selection. Restarting, returning to the menu, and refreshing unfinished rounds keep the current course.

title: More sensitive touch steering
summary: Much smaller swipes now give full steering in Slide Between.
changes: Increased drag steering sensitivity by roughly four times and reduced the dead zone.

title: Slide Between goes mobile
summary: Drag to steer and tap Jump to leap from launch pads.
changes: Steer with one finger while tapping the large Jump button with another, on the slide or in the air.
Touch instructions, launch hints and a Pause button fit the mobile controls.
Slide Between now appears in the Mobile Friendly library tab.

title: Unlock Crazy Sort difficulties sooner
summary: New difficulty tiers now unlock at 50 points.
changes: Score 50 on Normal to unlock Hard, 50 on Hard to unlock Chaos, and 50 on Chaos to unlock Hyperchaos.
Existing best scores count toward the lower requirements.

title: Take the leap in Slide Between
summary: A 3D robot race through floating doors joins the second row of the library.
changes: Jump from launch pads and land farther down the slide to gain an advantage.
Choose robot difficulty and courses, with best winning times included in password saves.

title: Follow your requests
summary: Requests now have a full page, replies from Rhett, and progress updates.
changes: Send a request at the top of the Request page and find your previous requests underneath.
Rhett can reply and set requests to Unread, In Progress or Released from the Admin Tab.
Each reply or status change adds a notification to Request. Open the updated request to read it and clear those notifications.

title: The Boomkins are loose
summary: Crazy Sort joins the library with five difficulty levels and a cast of colorful cartoon bombs.
changes: Drag each Boomkin into its matching pen before its fuse expires.
Unlock Hard, Chaos and Hyperchaos with higher scores. Best scores and unlocks travel with password saves.

title: Car Spleef goes 3D
summary: Car Spleef 3D joins the library beside the original.
changes: Thirty floating arenas, three AI rivals, drifting and switchable cockpit / chase cameras.
Includes its own progress, password-save support and Rhett’s Choice quote.

title: Three more games in Rhett’s Choice
summary: Ricochet Club, Parcel Panic and Odd Hours join the daily rotation with Rhett’s quotes.
changes: All three games now have their own quote in Rhett’s Choice.

title: A steadier arcade floor
summary: Fixed a canvas resize bug that could flash the arcade floor blank.
changes: Unchanged resize notifications no longer clear the floor canvas. Real size changes redraw immediately, before the browser displays the next frame.
Zoom measures the stable outer viewport so scrollbar changes cannot feed back into canvas sizing. Hidden game panels keep their last complete frame.
Existing saves, business progress, artwork and gameplay are preserved.

title: Ricochet Club joins the collection
summary: Now playable from the main arcade library.
changes: A quiet club with no final table. Master twelve opening rooms, then bank through endless generated layouts with more obstacles, smaller targets and tighter shot budgets.
Existing progress and sound preferences carry over.

title: Parcel Panic joins the collection
summary: Now playable from the main arcade library.
changes: A little delivery depot with a very satisfying job: fit parcels into the van, dispatch full rows and columns, and build a streak. No timer. Just a good fit.
Existing progress and sound preferences carry over.

title: Odd Hours joins the collection
summary: Now playable from the main arcade library.
changes: Four cameras. Forty different anomalies. Watch a detailed museum through five increasingly strange night shifts, compare reference photos, and report what changes.
Existing progress and sound preferences carry over.

title: A suit made for the frontier
summary: A rebuilt astronaut, from the curved visor to the molded boot soles.
changes: Custom sculpted surfaces replace the astronaut’s block-shaped chest unit, backpack, boots and simple capsule limbs. The suit has tailored proportions, fabric folds and seams, a conformal life-support pack, corrugated hoses and articulated fingers.
A shaped helmet has a curved optical visor, recessed seals, a retaining rim, side latches and restrained camera-following head movement.

Reworked walking and running keep the stance sole near the ground while preserving the existing footstep cadence. The knees have floating shields; rover, jump and hand-held survey-tool poses blend smoothly.

Rigid detail is batched into 69 meshes; the suit uses original code-built geometry and a small local fabric texture. The new character is shared by Helios and the Real Solar System without changing saved progress.

title: Real worlds from orbit
summary: Solar System Scope maps bring the Real Solar System closer to life.
changes: New locally bundled Solar System Scope textures for Mercury, Venus, Earth, the Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and four dwarf planets. The pack’s dwarf-planet reconstructions are credited as artistic imagery.
Earth has photographic cloud patterns and night-side city lights; Venus has a separate cloud map, and Saturn has mapped rings. Other moons retain their spacecraft mosaics and original gap fills.
Orbital imagery smoothly blends into the playable terrain as you approach. Irregular shapes, physical ground and existing colonies remain intact.
Chromebook, PC and High use 512, 1024 and 2048-pixel Scope maps respectively. Textures are shared through detail changes, released when replaced, and filtered across longitude seams.

title: Every Solar world, refreshed
summary: New textures and geological character from Mercury to Eris.
changes: All 41 solid planets, dwarf planets and moons have dedicated surface maps and material finishes. Earth, the Moon and selected worlds use locally bundled NASA/JPL/USGS mosaics; the remaining bodies have original authored maps.

New physical impact basins, ice fractures, volcanic shields, dunes, canyon fields and equatorial ridges give each surface more character. Ground collision, building placement and landing use the same terrain.
Earth, Venus and Titan have separated, slowly moving cloud layers. Jupiter has lacy belts and white ovals, Saturn a polar hexagon, Uranus a pale cap, and Neptune dark storms and bright cirrus.

Close-up materials distinguish dusty regolith, rock, frost and ice. Distant microdetail fades to reduce shimmer; Chromebook uses smaller maps. Historical mosaic gaps blend into original terrain rather than blank patches.
Existing colonies, science, ships, separate expedition saves and tutorial access remain intact. Landed Solar ships settle onto the refreshed ground.

title: Worlds with their own silhouettes
summary: The Real Solar System now has elongated, lumpy and flattened bodies.
changes: Haumea has a stretched, flattened ice-dwarf shape. Phobos, Deimos, Hyperion, Proteus and Pluto’s small moons have distinct irregular silhouettes; Kerberos has two joined lobes.
Ceres, several icy moons and the gas/ice giants have gentle flattening. Giant rings keep their circular geometry.
Detailed and distant terrain use the same shape as walking, construction, altitude and landing collision. Existing landed saves settle onto the corrected surface without losing progress.

title: A whole new vehicle assembly building
summary: Pick up, snap, move and stage your own rockets in a new 3D hangar.
changes: Pick up complete branches, snap to stack nodes or surfaces, insert tanks into existing stacks, and use mirror or up to 8-way radial symmetry.
Move and rotate parts with 3D handles or exact values, change the craft root, undo/redo, search real model thumbnails and reuse saved subassemblies.
Stage engines and decouplers, adjust fuel loads, priority, crossfeed and thrust limits, and see the effect on mass, thrust and delta-v. These settings carry into actual flight.
All five ready-to-fly presets remain available. The editor has compact Chromebook controls and separate inspector, staging and engineering tabs.

title: Send Rhett a request
summary: A signed letter form and a private owner inbox.
changes: Request sits below Settings. Sign your name above the letter and send with the Request button beneath it.
After a successful send, the server enforces a two-minute wait. A failed send keeps your draft.
Secret games is now called Admin Tab. Its Request inbox lets Rhett read letters and see unread counts after signing in with the site owner account.

title: Your first space adventure, without getting stranded
summary: Explorer assist makes Rustbound 2 easier to learn and more forgiving.
changes: Explorer assist is recommended and enabled by default. Turn it off in the main menu for the full flying challenge.
Landing checks are optional: let autopilot land, or try the checks knowing a missed approach will be caught. Rough impacts keep your fuel.
Help & rescue explains the game in plain language, starts the guided base projects or a first moon flight, and offers free repairs with at least 40% fuel and no cooldown.
Fuel and destination stay visible while orbital readouts and manual controls can be expanded. Accidental steering keys and camera drags no longer interrupt assisted flight.
The same beginner options work in Helios and the Real Solar System, with existing colonies, cargo and separate saves preserved.

title: Autopilot without the power requirement
summary: Fly with an empty battery in both expeditions.
changes: Autopilot no longer requires or consumes electricity for travel, orbit insertion, wormhole approaches, station docking or landing.
Guided flights continue through empty batteries and resume when a zero-charge flight save is loaded.
Ship science instruments and other electrical systems still use power. Journal guidance, lessons and warnings now explain the change.

title: Type admin. Take control of your expedition.
summary: A hidden tools panel for Helios and the Real Solar System.
changes: Type admin while playing or in the main menu to open a panel that pauses the game. Escape closes it. Text fields keep normal typing.
Toggle infinite ship electricity, infinite fuel, and an invulnerable hull. Overrides work with custom craft and reset on the next launch.
Teleport your current ship to any solid world or a safe circular orbit, including gas and ice giants. Cargo, colonies and rover locations are preserved.
Repair and refill the ship, add 10,000 credits, or unlock the current expedition’s research. Helios and Solar saves remain separate.

title: A whole new expedition: the Real Solar System
summary: Start on Earth and build from Mercury to Eris, with an independent save.
changes: A new button on the right of the main menu opens Real Solar System mode; Return to Helios switches back.
Eight planets, all five recognized dwarf planets and 32 selected moons include the Galilean moons, Titan, Enceladus, Triton, Charon and Dysnomia.
The same factories, resources, research, shipyard and space stations work in this mode. Earth and the Moon have starter bases.
Distances, gravity and sizes are compressed for friendly journeys. All 41 solid worlds have their own surface styling and footsteps.
Solar and Helios expeditions save separately; both travel with your Arcade save password. In-game resets affect only the current expedition.

title: Far Horizons: five systems worth the journey
summary: A rebuilt outer frontier, new Brontes, and a richer night sky.
changes: Forty new celestial bodies include ten gas and ice giants, moon families, tilted dwarf orbits, and the Drift–Mote pair.
Each outer system now has fourteen destinations and twelve landable worlds. The full game has 71 landable worlds.
Outer worlds have new terrain, mineral palettes, resource seams, survey sites, and distinct footsteps.
Brontes has animated cloud belts, a spiral storm, polar vortices, and fine rings.
A clustered starfield and galactic dust give each system a different sky.
Journal > Stars adds a destination atlas, moon hierarchy, survey hints, and landing progress. Existing colonies and wormhole routes are preserved.

title: A fresh start, one game at a time
summary: Save Wiper is now available in Your saves.
changes: Choose any main-library or Archives game and confirm before clearing its progress.
Linked password saves update with the reset, while other games and preferences are kept.
Favorites, tracked playtime, and arcade achievements stay with you.

title: A new home for your arcade
summary: A fresh look, with more ways to explore your games and follow your progress.
changes: What’s New keeps update notes in one place.
Open Details on any game for a preview, controls, and session guide.
Your stats tracks time in games, launches, records, and arcade achievements.
Shared volume, reduced motion, and Chromebook options live in Settings.
Archives games can now join your favorites.

title: There’s always another heist
summary: The campaign now leads into endless randomized jobs, and every level is tougher.
changes: Endless heists unlock after campaign level 100.
New attempts have tighter routes, more obstacles, and extra patrols.
Later jobs include more cameras and lasers.
Saved endless jobs and retries keep their layouts.

title: Cargo Swing is in the library
summary: An endless balancing act on a moving ship.
changes: Uneven cargo weight makes the hull tilt.
Crates can slide, fall overboard, or capsize the ship.
New harbor artwork, sound effects, and original music.

title: The Grand Collection opens
summary: One hundred heists across ten chapters.
changes: New chapters introduce keycards, cameras, lasers, panels, vaults, smoke, and hiding spots.
Earn up to three stars on each campaign job.
New museum artwork, sound effects, and music.

title: Deep Signal leaves the workshop
summary: An endless dive through increasingly dangerous waters.
changes: Recover every salvage pod to descend to the next sector.
Sonar briefly reveals distant salvage.
New underwater graphics, clearer instruments, sound, and music.

title: More places to leave tire marks
summary: Twenty extra symmetrical maps join Car Spleef.
changes: Thirty layouts now make up the map pool.
Bumper-car collisions and drifting still decide who stays on the tiles.
